checklist.step: Open the quarterly reconciliation cycle and lock the extract inventory
actions: On workday 1 after quarter end, open the close calendar and start the REG-057-C09 reconciliation task for the quarter.
List every required extract on the inventory tab: claims paid, case reserves, claim counts, written/earned premium and in-force policy counts, by writing entity and line of business.
Confirm with the Policy Admin Ops Lead that all policy admin batch cycles for the quarter have completed and the month-end snapshot is frozen.
Record the snapshot date and batch run ids on the inventory tab.
checklist.done: the inventory tab lists every extract with a confirmed frozen snapshot date and batch run id.

checklist.step: Pull the policy admin extracts with control totals
actions: In the Policy Administration Platform run the quarter-end extract jobs for claims transactions, open case reserves, claim counts and premium, selecting the frozen quarter-end snapshot.
Capture for each extract the row count, sum of paid amounts, sum of case reserves and sum of written premium straight from the extract job log.
Post the control totals to the reconciliation workbook control tab and hand the files to the warehouse load.
Flag any extract whose job log shows rejected rows and report the reject file to the Data Quality Analyst.
checklist.done: every extract landed with job-log control totals posted and zero unexplained rejects.

checklist.step: Load extracts to the warehouse staging schema and prove completeness
actions: Load each extract into the reserving staging schema and rerun row counts and amount sums in SQL against the loaded tables.
Compare loaded totals to the extract job-log totals; any difference greater than zero rows or one currency unit blocks the load.
Rerun the load for any blocked file rather than patching rows by hand.
Stamp the load log with run date, loader id and pass/fail per file.
checklist.done: loaded warehouse totals equal extract job-log totals exactly, with a stamped load log.

checklist.step: Run the data quality rule set over the staged quarter
actions: Execute the reserving DQ rule pack: valid line-of-business codes, non-negative case reserves, claim open/close date logic, currency codes, and orphan claims with no matching policy.
Export the rule-failure report and classify each failure as data defect, timing item or accepted anomaly.
Send data defects back to the Policy Administration Analyst with the claim/policy numbers for source correction before the reconciliation proceeds.
Attach the final rule run report to the reconciliation workbook.
checklist.done: the DQ rule run is attached with every failure classified and defects dispatched for source correction.

checklist.step: Extract the reserving datasets from the actuarial platform
actions: In Milliman Arius open the current quarter project and export the input data summary: paid loss, case reserves, claim counts and earned premium by line and accident period.
Export the same measures from the prior quarter project to isolate movement in the quarter.
Record the Arius project name, data-as-of date and export date on the workbook source tab.
Confirm the Arius data-as-of date equals the policy admin snapshot date; stop and reload if they differ.
checklist.done: Arius exports for current and prior quarter are on file with matching as-of dates.

checklist.step: Reconcile claims measures line by line
actions: In the reconciliation workbook build the comparison grid: warehouse staging totals vs Arius input totals for paid loss, case reserves and claim counts, by writing entity and line of business.
Compute the difference and the difference as a percentage of that line's carried reserves.
Mark every line whose difference exceeds 0.5% of carried reserves or 50 claim counts as a break.
Carry known timing items (late-posted recoveries, reinsurance cessions in transit) on the standing-items tab with their expected clearance quarter.
checklist.done: the grid shows a computed difference for every line with breaks marked against the 0.5% threshold.

checklist.step: Reconcile premium and exposure measures
actions: Compare written and earned premium by line between the warehouse staging totals and the Arius earned premium inputs.
Tie in-force policy counts from the policy admin snapshot to the exposure base used in the frequency assumptions.
Mark premium differences above 0.5% of line earned premium as breaks.
Note any line where exposure movement is inconsistent with premium movement and refer it to the Pricing Actuary for comment.
checklist.done: premium and exposure are reconciled with breaks marked and inconsistent lines referred.

checklist.step: Investigate every break to a named root cause
actions: For each break, drill the warehouse staging tables to transaction level and identify the claims or policies driving the difference.
Ask the Claims Analyst to confirm any suspect claim postings (reopened claims, bulk adjustments, currency conversions) against the claim file.
Assign each break a root cause code: extract scope, mapping error, timing, source correction or actuarial dataset error.
Record the root cause, the resolving action and the owner on the break register with a due date inside the current close.
checklist.done: every break carries a root cause code, owner and due date on the break register.

checklist.step: Post corrections and re-run the affected reconciliation lines
actions: Where the actuarial dataset was wrong, correct the Arius input table for the affected line and re-import; never key manual overrides into the triangle cells.
Where the source was wrong, wait for the Policy Administration Analyst's source correction and re-extract that measure.
Re-run the comparison grid for corrected lines and confirm the break falls under the 0.5% threshold.
Log each correction with before/after values and the evidence reference.
checklist.done: corrected lines re-reconcile under threshold with before/after values logged.

checklist.step: Tie the reconciled reserve data to the general ledger
actions: In SAP S/4HANA run the quarter-end trial balance for the loss reserve and unearned premium accounts by company code.
Compare GL carried reserves to the reconciled case reserves plus booked IBNR from the reserving summary.
Document any GL-to-actuarial difference and confirm it equals the booked management margin or pending journal, with the journal number cited.
Attach the trial balance extract to the reconciliation workbook.
checklist.done: GL reserve balances tie to the reconciled actuarial data with every difference explained by a cited journal.

checklist.step: Assemble and review the quarterly reconciliation report
actions: Compile the reconciliation report: control totals, comparison grids, break register with dispositions, standing timing items and the GL tie-out.
Review the standing-items tab and challenge any item older than two quarters for escalation.
Confirm no break above threshold remains open and the report covers every writing entity and line.
Sign and date the report as reconciliation owner by workday 10.
checklist.done: a complete report is signed by the Reserving Actuary by workday 10 with no over-threshold break open.

checklist.step: Obtain the Appointed Actuary's reliance sign-off
actions: Review the signed reconciliation report as the data-reliance basis for the statutory actuarial opinion required with the BMA statutory financial return.
Query any residual break or aged standing item that could bias the technical provisions and record the response.
Sign the quarterly reliance memo stating the policy admin data is fit for use in the EBS technical provisions and statutory reserve lines.
For Q4, reference the memo explicitly in the actuarial opinion workpapers filed with the SFR by April 30.
checklist.done: a signed reliance memo exists for the quarter and, for Q4, is referenced in the opinion workpapers.

checklist.step: Log unresolved items as compliance exceptions
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any over-threshold break open past workday 10 or any quarter closed without both signatures.
Record the line of business, amount, root cause and the remediation owner from the break register.
Set a remediation date no later than the next quarter's workday 10 and link the issue to REG-057-C09.
Notify the Head of Compliance where an exception could affect the April 30 SFR filing.
checklist.done: every unresolved item is a tracked exception with owner, date and REG-057-C09 linkage.

checklist.step: File the reconciliation pack in the evidence repository
actions: Upload the signed report, extract control logs, DQ rule run, break register and reliance memo under REG-057/C09/<year>-Q<n>.
Apply the 10-year retention label and the read-only flag.
Verify the index entry is searchable by quarter, entity and line of business.
Record the repository link on the close-calendar task before closing it.
checklist.done: the pack is filed read-only under the 10-year label with the link recorded on the closed task.

checklist.step: Feed recurring data defects into governed remediation
actions: Review the quarter's root cause codes and identify any defect that has recurred across two or more quarters.
Open a remediation item with the Data Quality Manager naming the source field, the failing rule and the fix owner in the policy admin team.
Track the fix to a target quarter and require the Reserving Analyst to confirm the break class disappears after the fix.
Report recurring-defect status to the quarterly data governance forum.
checklist.done: recurring defects carry an owned remediation item with a target quarter and forum reporting.

testing.step: Build the population of required reconciliations
actions: List the reconciliations required for the year: four quarters times every Bermuda-registered writing entity, from the close calendar.
Pull the completed reconciliation packs filed under REG-057/C09 in the compliance evidence repository.
Compare required versus filed; any missing quarter-entity pack is an automatic exception.
testing.done: a required-vs-filed matrix exists with every gap listed as an exception.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the close calendar and SFR dates
actions: Check each pack's Reserving Actuary signature date against the workday-10 close deadline.
Check the Q4 pack and reliance memo pre-date the BMA statutory financial return submission date (due within 4 months of year end).
List late signatures and any Q4 memo dated after the SFR filing as exceptions.
testing.done: every pack's dates are verified against workday 10 and the SFR filing date.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of reconciliation lines
actions: Select 100% of Q4 lines plus a seeded random sample of 15 entity-line-quarter combinations from Q1-Q3, minimum 30 lines total.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
Ensure the sample includes every line that reported a break during the year.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all Q4 lines and every break line is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the reconciliation for sampled lines
actions: Independently query the warehouse staging tables for paid loss, case reserves, claim counts and earned premium for each sampled line.
Compare your totals to the pack's comparison grid without reading the pack's conclusions first.
Recompute the difference percentage against carried reserves and check the break/no-break call.
Record any grid figure you cannot reproduce as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled line has an independent recomputation matching the pack or a logged exception.

testing.step: Trace control totals to the policy admin extract logs
actions: For two sampled quarters, open the Policy Administration Platform extract job logs and read the row counts and amount sums.
Agree them to the control tab in the reconciliation workbook.
Confirm the snapshot date used matches the frozen quarter-end snapshot recorded on the inventory tab.
testing.done: job-log totals and snapshot dates agree with the workbook for both traced quarters.

testing.step: Recompute the break threshold and aging maths
actions: Recompute 0.5% of carried reserves for each sampled line and verify the break flagging was arithmetically right.
Age every break on the year's break registers and verify none stayed open past the following quarter's workday 10 without a tracker exception.
Recheck standing timing items cleared in their stated clearance quarter.
testing.done: threshold and aging arithmetic verifies clean or the failures are logged.

testing.step: Verify the GL tie-out to SAP
actions: Rerun the quarter-end trial balance for reserve accounts for one sampled quarter in SAP S/4HANA.
Agree GL balances to the pack's tie-out and re-verify each cited reconciling journal exists with the stated amount.
Trace the booked IBNR figure to the reserving summary signed by the Reserving Actuary.
testing.done: GL balances, journals and IBNR all trace cleanly for the sampled quarter.

testing.step: Verify sign-off integrity and segregation
actions: Check each pack carries both the Reserving Actuary signature and the Appointed Actuary reliance memo.
Confirm the preparer of the workbook is not the signer of the reliance memo.
Confirm the Q4 reliance memo is referenced in the actuarial opinion workpapers supporting the SFR.
testing.done: all packs show segregated preparer/signer and the Q4 memo links into the opinion workpapers.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception citing the quarter, entity, line and the failed attribute.
Assign a root cause (missing pack, late sign-off, irreproducible figure, untracked break) and a named remediation owner.
Set remediation dates and mark any exception touching the filed SFR for Head of Compliance review.
Carry open exceptions into next year's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception is tracked with root cause, owner, date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-missing-reconciliation threshold and state a conclusion: effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective.
Have the Chief Audit Executive, who performed none of the reconciliations, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Audit Committee and the Appointed Actuary before the next SFR cycle.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-057/C09/testing.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to the Audit Committee.

In-scope systems.value: Regulator correspondence case queue; source valuation data pulled from the actuarial platform; final letters filed in the correspondence file

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Actuary and General Counsel; reviewed annually after the SFR filing season

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per inquiry — the response date stated in the BMA letter governs; where none is stated the internal standard is 14 calendar days from receipt, mirroring the Act's 14-day notification convention

checklist.step: Log every inbound valuation inquiry the day it arrives
actions: Monitor the BMA relationship mailbox and the principal representative's inbox daily for supervisory letters and e-mail queries.
Open a case the same day with: BMA reference number, receipt date, the filing it concerns (SFR year, BSCR schedule, EBS line), and the response date stated in the letter.
Where no date is stated, set the due date to receipt plus 14 calendar days per the procedure.
Attach the inbound letter PDF to the case and notify the Appointed Actuary.
checklist.done: the case exists same-day with BMA reference, governing due date and the letter attached.

checklist.step: Acknowledge receipt to the BMA within 2 business days
actions: Send a written acknowledgement to the BMA supervisor named in the letter, quoting the BMA reference number and confirming the response date.
Where the stated deadline is unachievable, request an extension in the same acknowledgement, stating the reason and a committed alternate date.
File the acknowledgement (and any extension grant) on the case.
Update the case due date only when the BMA confirms the extension in writing.
checklist.done: a filed acknowledgement exists within 2 business days and the case due date matches the BMA-confirmed date.

checklist.step: Triage the inquiry and assign a single response owner
actions: Read the inquiry and classify it: data clarification, methodology challenge, assumption support, or potential deficiency finding.
Assign a drafting owner — Valuation Actuary for EBS/technical-provision questions, Reserving Actuary for triangle and IBNR questions.
Flag potential-deficiency classifications to General Counsel immediately, before any drafting starts.
Record the classification and owner on the case.
checklist.done: the case shows a classification, a named drafting owner and, where flagged, a counsel notification.

checklist.step: Reconstruct the exact filed figures under question
actions: Pull the as-filed SFR, BSCR schedule or EBS exhibit from the financial reporting repository for the year in question.
Trace each questioned figure to its workpaper: model run id, assumption set version and data as-of date.
Verify the figure in the filing matches the workpaper output; note any transcription difference immediately.
List the source references on the case so the response can cite them precisely.
checklist.done: every questioned figure traces to a named workpaper, model run and assumption version.

checklist.step: Re-run or re-derive the questioned valuation figures
actions: Re-open the archived model run in the actuarial platform using the archived assumption set and data snapshot.
Re-produce the questioned outputs and compare to the filed figures to confirm reproducibility.
Where the BMA asks for sensitivities, run the requested scenario with only the named parameter changed and log the run id.
Export the supporting exhibits the response will attach.
checklist.done: filed figures are reproduced from archived runs and any requested sensitivity has a logged run id.

checklist.step: Draft the response answering each question in the BMA's own numbering
actions: Structure the draft to mirror the BMA letter question by question, quoting each question before its answer.
Cite the specific filing line, schedule and workpaper reference behind every figure given.
State assumptions and judgements explicitly, including where the answer relies on the Appointed Actuary's professional judgement.
Keep to the questions asked — no volunteered analysis beyond scope without Appointed Actuary agreement.
checklist.done: a draft exists answering every numbered question with filing-line and workpaper citations.

checklist.step: Second-actuary technical review of the draft
actions: Have an actuary who did not draft the response verify every figure in the draft against the exported exhibits.
Check internal consistency with prior BMA correspondence and the filed actuarial opinion — contradictions are found now, not by the regulator.
Re-check any day-count or threshold arithmetic quoted in the draft.
Record the review outcome and reviewer name on the case.
checklist.done: an independent actuarial reviewer has verified figures and consistency, recorded on the case.

checklist.step: Legal clearance before signature
actions: Review the draft for admissions, undertakings and privilege issues, especially where a valuation error or restatement is conceded.
Confirm any commitment offered (a refiling, a methodology change, a future report) is one the company can honour by the stated date.
Mark required wording changes directly and return the draft within 2 business days.
Record clearance on the case; no response leaves without it.
checklist.done: written legal clearance is on the case and all counsel edits are incorporated.

checklist.step: Appointed Actuary sign-off on the final response
actions: Read the final response end to end against the BMA letter and the reviewed exhibits.
Sign as the actuary responsible for the valuation, dating the signature.
Confirm the response can be filed as an annex to next year's opinion workpapers without contradiction.
Authorize transmission on the case.
checklist.done: the final response carries the Appointed Actuary's dated signature and transmission authority.

checklist.step: Transmit the response to the BMA before the due date
actions: Send the signed response and exhibits to the BMA supervisor via the channel the BMA used (its e-filing portal upload or the named supervisor's e-mail), quoting the BMA reference number.
Send no later than the case due date; a same-day internal escalation to the CFO fires if transmission would be late.
Capture the transmission timestamp and any BMA delivery confirmation.
Set a 10-business-day follow-up task to confirm the BMA received and accepted the response.
checklist.done: the response is transmitted on or before the due date with a captured timestamp and follow-up task.

checklist.step: File the complete correspondence set
actions: File under REG-057/C10/<BMA reference>: inbound letter, acknowledgement, data pulls, draft with review marks, legal clearance, signed response and transmission proof.
Apply the 10-year retention label.
Index the folder by BMA reference number, filing year and topic.
Link the folder to the case before moving the case to 'Awaiting BMA closure'.
checklist.done: a complete indexed correspondence folder exists with 10-year retention and case linkage.

checklist.step: Track every commitment made in the response
actions: Extract each undertaking from the signed response (refile a schedule, amend a methodology, report back by a date) into its own tracker item.
Assign each item the owner named in the response and the committed date.
Alert the Appointed Actuary at T-14 and T-7 before each committed date.
Close items only with evidence the commitment was delivered to the BMA.
checklist.done: every commitment is a tracked item with owner, date, reminders and delivery evidence at closure.

checklist.step: Confirm BMA closure and record the outcome
actions: Follow up with the BMA supervisor if no reaction arrives within 30 days of the response.
Record the BMA's closure note, further-question letter or finding on the case.
Reopen the workflow from the triage step for any follow-up questions, under the same BMA reference.
Mark the case closed only on written BMA closure or 90 days of silence after a follow-up.
checklist.done: the case shows a recorded BMA outcome or a documented 90-day closure basis.

checklist.step: Feed findings back into the valuation process
actions: Review closed inquiries quarterly for methodology or disclosure weaknesses the BMA has flagged.
Direct changes to the valuation procedure, assumption documentation or SFR disclosure templates where a question exposed a gap.
Brief the Audit Committee on any inquiry classified as a potential deficiency and its resolution.
Record the process change and its effective valuation cycle.
checklist.done: quarterly review minutes show each BMA-flagged weakness mapped to a process change or a reasoned no-change.

checklist.step: Escalate deadline risk before it becomes a breach
actions: Review the case queue weekly for inquiries inside 5 days of due date without a signed draft.
Escalate at-risk cases to the Appointed Actuary and CFO the same day with the blocking issue named.
Ensure an extension request goes to the BMA before the due date, never after.
Record the escalation and outcome on the case.
checklist.done: no case passes its due date without either a transmitted response or a pre-deadline extension request.

testing.step: Build the population of valuation inquiries for the year
actions: Extract all cases tagged 'regulator valuation inquiry' opened in the test year from the case queue, with receipt dates, due dates and transmission dates.
Record case counts by classification and by quarter.
Export the list to the test workpaper as the primary population.
testing.done: a dated case extract with receipt, due and transmission dates forms the population.

testing.step: Sweep for inquiries that never reached the queue
actions: Search the BMA relationship mailbox and the principal representative's inbox for the year for senders at bma.bm and subjects citing the SFR, BSCR or EBS.
Match every hit to a case in the population extract.
List any BMA letter with no matching case as an automatic completeness exception.
testing.done: every BMA valuation e-mail or letter found maps to a case or is an exception.

testing.step: Draw the sample
actions: Take 100% of cases classified as potential deficiency plus a seeded random sample of the remainder, minimum 10 cases or the whole population if smaller.
Record seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
Include at least one case from each quarter with activity.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all deficiency-class cases is documented.

testing.step: Recompute timeliness on every sampled case
actions: Recompute acknowledgement date minus receipt date and compare to the 2-business-day standard.
Recompute transmission date against the BMA-stated date or receipt plus 14 calendar days, honouring only BMA-confirmed extensions.
List every late acknowledgement or late response as an exception with the day count.
testing.done: day-count arithmetic is recomputed for every sampled case with lates listed.

testing.step: Verify the response answered what was asked
actions: Read the inbound BMA letter and the signed response side by side for each sampled case.
Confirm every numbered question has a substantive answer with a filing-line or workpaper citation.
Flag any question answered by omission or by generic narrative as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled response maps one-to-one to the BMA's questions or exceptions are logged.

testing.step: Re-perform the figure support for one sampled case
actions: For the highest-impact sampled case, open the archived model run cited in the response.
Reproduce two figures quoted to the BMA from the archived run outputs.
Compare to the letter; any figure not reproducible from the cited run is an exception.
Capture the run id and output screens into the workpaper.
testing.done: quoted figures reproduce from the cited archived run with evidence captured.

testing.step: Verify review and clearance controls operated
actions: Check each sampled case for the second-actuary review record, the General Counsel clearance and the Appointed Actuary's dated signature.
Confirm the drafting owner and the second reviewer are different people.
Any response transmitted without all three records is an exception.
testing.done: all sampled cases show segregated review, legal clearance and signed authority, or exceptions are logged.

testing.step: Trace commitments to delivery
actions: List every commitment extracted from sampled responses and find its tracker item.
Verify closure evidence shows delivery to the BMA by the committed date.
List missing tracker items or late deliveries as exceptions.
testing.done: every sampled commitment traces to a tracked, evidenced, on-time delivery or an exception.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise one issue per exception citing the BMA reference and failed attribute.
Assign root cause (mailbox miss, SLA overrun, missing clearance, irreproducible figure) and a named owner.
Set remediation dates; route any late-response breach to General Counsel for regulatory-relations assessment.
Carry open items to next year's test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception carries root cause, owner, date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude and obtain independent sign-off
actions: State the conclusion against the zero-unlogged, zero-late threshold: effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective.
Have the Chief Audit Executive, who touched none of the responses, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Audit Committee and the Appointed Actuary.
File the signed workpaper under REG-057/C10/testing in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed, filed workpaper states the conclusion and committee reporting date.

checklist.step: Maintain the definitive board and committee register
actions: Keep the register current in the board portal: each body (board, audit committee, risk committee), its members, roles, independence status, appointment date and term end.
Update the register within 5 business days of any appointment, resignation or role change, sourcing the change from the signed board resolution.
Cross-check quarterly against the register of directors and officers filed with the Bermuda Registrar of Companies.
Flag any body whose membership falls below its charter minimum to the Board Governance Lead the same day.
checklist.done: the register matches signed resolutions and the Registrar filing, with no unflagged under-strength body.

checklist.step: Keep every charter current and board-approved
actions: Each Q1, open every charter in the board portal document library and check its last approval date is within 12 months.
Redline charters against the current BMA Insurance Code of Conduct governance paragraphs and any new BMA guidance notes.
Route redlines to General Counsel for review, then to the full board for approval as a minuted resolution.
Replace the portal master copy with the approved version, dated and version-numbered.
checklist.done: every charter shows a board approval within 12 months and reflects current Code of Conduct text.

checklist.step: Verify composition against the Code of Conduct matrix
actions: Complete the composition matrix each quarter: independent non-executive count, audit committee independence and financial expertise, risk committee coverage, and separation of chair/CEO where required.
Test each member's independence against the criteria (no material business relationship, tenure, cross-directorships) and record the basis.
Confirm the skills matrix covers insurance, actuarial, audit and Bermuda regulatory expertise per Schedule 2's adequate-knowledge criterion.
Present gaps to the nomination discussion with a refill timeline no longer than 90 days.
checklist.done: a completed quarterly matrix shows compliant composition or a gap with an owned refill plan under 90 days.

checklist.step: Plan the annual meeting calendar to satisfy cadence and head-office rules
actions: Schedule at minimum quarterly board meetings and each committee's charter-mandated cadence for the year ahead in the board portal calendar.
Locate enough board meetings in Bermuda, with the principal representative attending, to evidence direction and management from Bermuda under s.8B.
Align the Q1 board meeting to approve the statutory financial statements before the SFR filing date (within 4 months of year end).
Circulate the calendar to all directors and the Chief Executive Officer.
checklist.done: a published calendar meets cadence, Bermuda-presence and SFR-approval timing requirements.

checklist.step: Run each meeting with quorum and agenda discipline
actions: Issue the pack through the board portal at least 5 business days before each meeting, with agenda items mapped to charter responsibilities.
At meeting open, count attendance against the charter quorum and record names, locations and dial-in status in the minutes.
If quorum fails, adjourn, minute the failure and reschedule within 10 business days.
Track charter-mandated standing items (risk appetite review, auditor private session) so none is skipped in the year.
checklist.done: each meeting shows a timely pack, a minuted quorum count and standing items tracked to completion.

checklist.step: Minute decisions to an evidential standard
actions: Draft minutes within 10 business days capturing decisions, dissents, conflicts declared and management actions with owners and dates.
Circulate draft minutes to the chair for review and table them for approval at the next meeting.
Store approved minutes as locked PDFs in the board portal minute book.
Extract action items into the follow-up log with owner and due date.
checklist.done: approved, locked minutes exist for every meeting with actions extracted to the follow-up log.

checklist.step: Track board and committee actions to closure
actions: Load every minuted action into the follow-up log with body, meeting date, owner and due date.
Chase owners at T-10 and T-3 before due dates and collect closure evidence.
Report overdue actions to the relevant chair at each meeting via the pack's action-log page.
Close actions only with evidence attached.
checklist.done: the action log shows every minuted action closed with evidence or visibly overdue to its chair.

checklist.step: Evidence direction and management from Bermuda
actions: Maintain the s.8B head-office evidence file: where board and executive decisions are taken, where senior executives who make day-to-day decisions reside, and the Bermuda meeting record.
Log each Bermuda-held meeting with location and attendee residency.
Review the file with General Counsel each Q4 against the BMA's head-office guidance factors.
Correct the forward calendar if the Bermuda meeting count is trending short.
checklist.done: the head-office file demonstrates the s.8B factors with a Q4 counsel review on record.

checklist.step: Onboard every new director into the required structures
actions: Deliver the induction pack: Insurance Act 1978 duties, Code of Conduct obligations, charters, the composition matrix and the current risk appetite statement.
Book the new director's fitness-and-propriety file with HR/Legal before first attendance (see REG-057-C13).
Record completion of induction in the director register within 30 days of appointment.
Update committee memberships by minuted resolution, never by informal invitation.
checklist.done: each new director shows a completed induction, an F&P file and a minuted committee assignment.

checklist.step: Notify the BMA of relevant officer and director changes
actions: On any change of director or officer, prepare the s.30 notification to the BMA with the effective date and the replacement plan.
File the notification within 45 days of the change, or sooner where the BMA's conditions on the insurer require it.
Where the change removes a Schedule 2-relevant function holder, state the interim cover arrangement in the notification.
File the BMA acknowledgement in the director register.
checklist.done: every change carries a timely s.30 notification with the BMA acknowledgement filed.

checklist.step: Run the annual board and committee effectiveness evaluation
actions: Issue the Q4 evaluation questionnaire through the board portal covering charter adherence, information quality, cadence sufficiency and Code of Conduct alignment.
Compile results and present them to the full board with proposed structural changes.
Minute the accepted changes and feed them into the Q1 charter review.
Engage an external evaluator at least every third year and file the report.
checklist.done: a minuted annual evaluation exists with accepted changes routed into the charter cycle.

checklist.step: Certify the governance basis for the Declaration of Compliance
actions: Before the SFR filing, review the year's register, matrix, minutes and exception log against Schedule 2 minimum criteria.
Prepare the internal certification supporting the s.8A Declaration of Compliance for the two signing directors.
List any open governance exception on the certification with its remediation state, so signatories decide with full knowledge.
File the certification with the SFR workpapers.
checklist.done: a pre-SFR certification exists, exception-complete, supporting the signed Declaration of Compliance.

checklist.step: Log and remediate governance exceptions
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any quorum failure, lapsed charter, missed mandatory meeting or composition breach on the day it is identified.
Assign root cause and a remediation owner; composition breaches get a refill plan with a date under 90 days.
Obtain Board Governance Lead sign-off at closure, plus minuted board-chair acknowledgement for composition breaches.
Review open exceptions monthly with the Corporate Secretary.
checklist.done: every exception is tracked, owned, and closed with the required sign-offs.

checklist.step: Archive the governance record set
actions: Each January, archive the prior year's charters, matrices, minutes, attendance registers and evaluation report under REG-057/C11/<year>.
Apply the 10-year retention label and read-only flag.
Verify retrieval by body, date and document type.
Note the archive location in the governance calendar's year-close task.
checklist.done: the prior year's full governance record is archived read-only under 10-year retention.

checklist.step: Brief the board on regulatory governance developments
actions: Monitor BMA consultation papers, Code of Conduct amendments and Insurance Act amendment bills each quarter.
Summarize governance-relevant changes in a board pack item with a gap assessment against current structures.
Obtain a board decision on required structural changes and route them into the charter and matrix processes.
Record the review date even when no change is required.
checklist.done: each quarter's pack contains a regulatory-development item with a minuted decision or nil-return.

testing.step: Build the population of bodies, meetings and changes
actions: Extract from the board portal the year's meeting calendar (held and cancelled), the charter library with approval dates, and the director register change history.
Count meetings per body against charter-mandated cadence.
Record the population in the test workpaper.
testing.done: the workpaper holds the full-year meeting, charter and change population.

testing.step: Reconcile the register to external sources of record
actions: Agree the director register to the Bermuda Registrar of Companies filing and to the signed appointment/resignation resolutions.
Agree committee memberships to the minuted resolutions that created them.
List any member serving without a resolution, or any register/Registrar mismatch, as an exception.
testing.done: the register reconciles to resolutions and the Registrar filing or exceptions are listed.

testing.step: Draw the meeting sample
actions: Select every board meeting plus a seeded random sample of 6 committee meetings across audit and risk committees.
Record seed, population and selection date.
Include any meeting minuted as quorum-failed or rescheduled.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all board meetings and failure cases is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the quorum and cadence checks
actions: For each sampled meeting, read the minuted attendance and recount quorum against the charter in force on that date.
Verify the year contained at least one board meeting per quarter and each committee met its charter cadence.
Verify packs were issued at least 5 business days ahead from the portal distribution timestamps.
Log any recount that contradicts the minutes as an exception.
testing.done: quorum, cadence and pack timing verify for every sampled meeting or exceptions are logged.

testing.step: Verify charter currency and approval trail
actions: For each charter, trace the current version to the board minute approving it and check the approval is within 12 months.
Spot-check two charters against the current BMA Insurance Code of Conduct paragraphs for the mandated content.
List any charter without a minuted, in-date approval as an exception.
testing.done: every charter traces to an in-date minuted approval with content spot-checks passed.

testing.step: Re-perform the composition matrix for year end
actions: Independently rebuild the year-end composition matrix from the register: independence counts, expertise coverage and chair/CEO separation.
Compare to the Q4 matrix the Board Governance Lead produced.
Recompute the age of any open composition gap against the 90-day threshold.
testing.done: the rebuilt matrix matches the Q4 matrix and no gap exceeded 90 days untracked.

testing.step: Test the s.8B head-office evidence
actions: Count Bermuda-held board meetings from the minuted locations and compare to the head-office file's claim.
Verify the principal representative's attendance at those meetings from the attendance registers.
Confirm the Q4 counsel review of the file happened and is documented.
testing.done: the head-office file's claims reproduce from minutes and attendance records.

testing.step: Trace officer/director changes to s.30 notifications
actions: For every change in the register history, find the s.30 notification to the BMA and its acknowledgement.
Recompute days from effective change to notification against the 45-day standard.
List unnotified or late-notified changes as exceptions for General Counsel review.
testing.done: every change traces to a timely acknowledged notification or a logged exception.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise one issue per exception with body, date and failed attribute.
Assign root cause (register lapse, calendar slip, notification miss) and an owner in the Corporate Secretariat.
Set remediation dates and flag anything touching the signed Declaration of Compliance to General Counsel.
Carry open items into next year's test.
testing.done: all exceptions are tracked with root cause, owner, date and escalation where required.

testing.step: Conclude with independent sign-off and report
actions: State the conclusion against the thresholds (no charterless committee, no unminuted quorum failure, no >90-day composition gap).
Have the Chief Audit Executive sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report to the audit committee ahead of the Declaration of Compliance signing.
File the workpaper under REG-057/C11/testing in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed conclusion is filed and reported before the Declaration of Compliance is signed.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the governance-disclosure filing calendar: the Bermuda s.8A Declaration of Compliance with the SFR, group governance filings to the BMA, and US lead-state CGAD/holding-company forms where the group writes US business

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Insurance Act 1978 s.8A (Declaration of Compliance), s.17/s.18 (statutory financial return it accompanies) and s.27F group supervision provisions, plus the lead state's CGAD statute for US entities, re-verified each January when the filing calendar is built

In-scope processes.value: Annual and event-driven governance filings: Declaration of Compliance signed by two directors with the SFR (due within 4 months of year end), BMA group governance submissions, and CGAD/Form B holding-company filings for US-licensed affiliates by the lead state's June 1 convention

In-scope systems.value: Governance filing calendar and status board; source documents drawn from the board portal; filed copies in the compliance evidence repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Governance Disclosure Filing Procedure — filing inventory per jurisdiction, drafting owners, director sign-off flow for the s.8A Declaration, transmission channels and confirmation capture

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by General Counsel and the Chief Financial Officer; reviewed each January against new BMA and lead-state requirements

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Declaration of Compliance travels with the SFR (April 30 for a December 31 year end); CGAD by the lead state's June 1 date; event-driven holding-company amendments within the state's stated window; BMA notifications within 14 days where the Act so provides

checklist.step: Build the annual governance filing inventory
actions: Each January, list every governance disclosure due in the year: s.8A Declaration of Compliance per Bermuda-registered entity, BMA group governance submissions, and CGAD/holding-company forms per US-licensed affiliate with its lead state named.
Enter each filing on the tracker with jurisdiction, statutory cite, due date, drafting owner and signatory requirements.
Confirm the SFR filing date with the Regulatory Reporting Manager so the Declaration slot aligns (within 4 months of year end).
Have General Counsel confirm the inventory is complete against current statutes before locking it.
checklist.done: a counsel-confirmed inventory with owners and due dates is locked on the tracker.

checklist.step: Set reminder ladders and signature logistics
actions: Configure T-60/T-30/T-14/T-7 reminders on every inventory line, addressed to the drafting owner and Corporate Secretary.
Book the two director signature slots for the s.8A Declaration three weeks before the SFR date, using directors physically available to sign.
Record backup signatories in case a booked director becomes unavailable.
Verify reminder delivery by test-firing one reminder per quarter-cohort.
checklist.done: reminders are live on every line and Declaration signature slots are booked with backups.

checklist.step: Compile the compliance basis for the Declaration of Compliance
actions: Assemble the s.8A support file: minimum-margin and enhanced-capital evidence from Capital Management, governance certification from General Counsel (REG-057-C11), and the exception log for the year.
Obtain from the Capital Management Manager written confirmation that the entity met its solvency margins and capital requirements at year end.
List every open exception that a signing director should weigh, with its remediation state.
Deliver the file to the signing directors at least 10 business days before the signature slot.
checklist.done: signing directors hold a complete support file 10 business days before signing.

checklist.step: Draft the Declaration of Compliance in the prescribed form
actions: Draft the Declaration on the BMA's current prescribed form, covering the entity's compliance with the minimum criteria, solvency margin and applicable conditions for the financial year.
Verify entity legal name, registration class and financial year end against the certificate of registration.
Note any non-compliance the support file surfaced and draft the required qualification wording with General Counsel.
Version the draft in the document management repository.
checklist.done: a prescribed-form draft exists, entity details verified, with any qualification wording settled.

checklist.step: Obtain two director signatures on the Declaration
actions: Route the final Declaration to the two booked directors via DocuSign with the support file attached.
Confirm each signatory is a director of the declaring entity on the signature date, per the director register.
Capture both signatures and the completion certificate at least 5 business days before the SFR filing date.
Store the executed Declaration with the DocuSign envelope id.
checklist.done: the Declaration bears two verified director signatures captured ahead of the SFR date.

checklist.step: File the Declaration with the statutory financial return
actions: Attach the executed Declaration to the SFR package in the BMA's electronic filing portal in the slot the portal provides for the s.8A Declaration.
Submit within the SFR deadline — 4 months after financial year end, or the BMA-approved extended date.
Download the portal submission receipt showing date, time and package contents.
Update the tracker line to Filed with the receipt attached.
checklist.done: the portal receipt shows the Declaration filed inside the deadline and the tracker reflects it.

checklist.step: Prepare the CGAD for each US-licensed affiliate
actions: Update last year's Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure against the year's actual changes: board composition, committee structures, senior management changes and remuneration governance.
Pull the change list from the director register and REG-057-C11 evaluation outputs rather than re-writing from memory.
Confirm with the Regulatory Affairs Manager which affiliate files with which lead state and whether the state accepts a group-level CGAD.
Route the draft to General Counsel and the affiliate board for the required signature.
checklist.done: a signed, change-accurate CGAD exists per affiliate with the lead state confirmed.

checklist.step: File the CGAD with the lead state by June 1
actions: Submit the CGAD through the lead state's designated channel — its regulator portal upload or the filing e-mail its instructions name — by the state's June 1 convention or its stated alternate date.
Mark the filing confidential per the CGAD model act protections in the transmittal.
Capture the state's confirmation of receipt.
Update the tracker line with the confirmation attached.
checklist.done: each CGAD is confirmed received by its lead state on or before the due date.

checklist.step: Monitor for events that trigger holding-company or BMA notifications
actions: Watch board resolutions, M&A activity and control changes monthly for triggers: change of shareholder controller, material intra-group agreements, or amendments to registered particulars.
For Bermuda triggers, prepare the BMA notification and file within the Act's stated window — 14 days where s.30-type notification applies.
For US triggers, prepare the Form B amendment or Form A consultation with outside counsel where control thresholds are approached.
Log each trigger assessment on the tracker even when the conclusion is no filing required, with the reasoning.
checklist.done: every trigger event shows a filed notification or a reasoned no-filing record inside its window.

checklist.step: Quality-check every filing package before transmission
actions: Run the pre-transmission checklist: correct prescribed form version, entity details, signatures present and dated, attachments complete, confidentiality markings applied.
Compare the package against the prior year's accepted filing for structural drift.
Reject packages back to the drafting owner rather than fixing in transmission.
Initial the checklist and file it with the package.
checklist.done: an initialled pre-transmission checklist exists for every filed package.

checklist.step: Capture and file all transmission proofs
actions: For each filing, store the signed instrument, portal receipt or transmission e-mail, and any regulator acknowledgement under REG-057/C12/<year>/<filing>.
Apply the 10-year retention label.
Record the repository link on the tracker line before closing it.
Verify quarterly that no closed line lacks its proof set.
checklist.done: every closed filing line links to a complete, retention-labelled proof folder.

checklist.step: Respond to regulator questions on a filed disclosure
actions: Log any BMA or state query about a governance filing as a case with the regulator's stated response date, defaulting to 14 days where none is given.
Draft the response from the filed instrument and its support file, never from memory.
Obtain General Counsel clearance where the query implies a deficiency in the filed disclosure.
File the query and response in the same folder as the original filing.
checklist.done: each query is logged, answered on time with clearance, and filed alongside the original.

checklist.step: Handle a discovered error in a filed disclosure
actions: On discovery of a material error, assess with the Corporate Secretary whether the instrument must be refiled or corrected by letter.
Notify the BMA or lead state proactively with the corrected instrument and an explanation, rather than waiting for challenge.
Log the error as an exception with root cause and the correction evidence.
Brief the signing directors on any correction to a Declaration they signed.
checklist.done: any filed error is proactively corrected, logged and briefed to its signatories.

checklist.step: Close the filing year and roll the inventory
actions: At year end, verify every inventory line shows Filed with proof or a documented not-due rationale.
Summarize the year's filings, lates and exceptions in a one-page report to the audit committee.
Roll the inventory to the new year, updating due dates and any statutory changes counsel identifies.
Archive the closed year's tracker view to the evidence repository.
checklist.done: the year closes with all lines resolved, a committee report delivered and the new inventory rolled.

checklist.step: Track regulatory change affecting governance disclosures
actions: Review BMA consultation papers and lead-state bulletin feeds quarterly for changes to the Declaration form, CGAD content or holding-company forms.
Assess each change for effect on the inventory, forms or due dates and record the assessment.
Update the procedure and inventory before the next filing cycle where a change lands.
Report material changes to General Counsel and the Corporate Secretary within the quarter.
checklist.done: quarterly change reviews are recorded and the inventory reflects every landed change.

testing.step: Build the population from the filing inventory
actions: Extract the year's locked inventory with due dates, owners and status from the tracker.
Independently rebuild the required-filing list from statute: one s.8A Declaration per Bermuda entity, CGAD per US affiliate lead state, plus trigger-driven filings from the year's board resolutions.
Compare the rebuilt list to the inventory; any missing required filing is an automatic exception.
testing.done: an independently rebuilt required list reconciles to the inventory or gaps are exceptions.

testing.step: Reconcile filed status to transmission proofs
actions: For every line marked Filed, open the proof folder and verify the signed instrument, receipt and acknowledgement exist.
Match the receipt's entity, form and period to the inventory line.
List any Filed line without a complete proof set as an exception.
testing.done: every Filed line is evidenced by a complete proof folder or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Recompute timeliness on every filing
actions: Recompute each Declaration's filing date against year end plus 4 months (or the BMA-approved extension on file).
Recompute each CGAD date against the lead state's June 1 convention or its stated alternate.
Recompute trigger-driven notifications against their statutory windows, including the 14-day cases.
List every late day-count as an exception with the overrun.
testing.done: every filing's day-count is recomputed with lates quantified.

testing.step: Verify Declaration signature validity
actions: For each s.8A Declaration, verify two signatures exist and each signatory was a director of the declaring entity on the signature date per the director register.
Verify the DocuSign completion certificate matches the filed instrument.
Any Declaration with fewer than two valid director signatures is a reportable breach, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every Declaration shows two register-verified director signatures matching the filed copy.

testing.step: Re-perform the support-file check for one Declaration
actions: For one sampled entity, re-open the support file behind the signed Declaration.
Verify the solvency confirmation from Capital Management and the governance certification were dated before signature.
Check every exception open at signature date was disclosed to the signatories in the file.
An undisclosed open exception is an exception of this test.
testing.done: the sampled Declaration's support file is complete, pre-dated and exception-transparent.

testing.step: Verify CGAD content against source records
actions: For one sampled CGAD, agree the disclosed board composition and committee structure to the year-end director register.
Agree disclosed governance changes to the REG-057-C11 evaluation outputs and minutes.
Flag any disclosure that contradicts the register or minutes.
testing.done: the sampled CGAD's content reconciles to the register and minutes.

testing.step: Test trigger-event completeness
actions: Read the year's board and committee minutes for control changes, material intra-group agreements and registered-particular amendments.
Match each identified trigger to a tracker assessment record.
List any trigger with no assessment as an exception regardless of whether a filing was ultimately due.
testing.done: every minute-identified trigger maps to a documented assessment.

testing.step: Verify query and correction handling
actions: List regulator queries and self-identified corrections from the year and open each folder.
Verify responses met the logged response dates and carried General Counsel clearance where deficiencies were implied.
Verify corrections were proactively notified with the corrected instrument on file.
testing.done: all queries and corrections show timely, cleared, evidenced handling.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the filing, jurisdiction and failed attribute.
Assign root cause (inventory gap, signature logistics, deadline miss, proof gap) and an owner.
Route signature-validity and unfiled-Declaration findings to General Counsel same-day.
Set remediation dates and carry open items to next year's test.
testing.done: every exception is tracked with root cause, owner and escalation where required.

testing.step: Conclude with independent sign-off
actions: State the conclusion against the zero-unfiled, zero-late threshold: effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective.
Have the Chief Audit Executive, uninvolved in any filing, sign the workpaper.
Report to the audit committee and the Corporate Secretary before the next inventory build.
File the workpaper under REG-057/C12/testing.
testing.done: a signed, filed conclusion is reported ahead of the next filing cycle.

checklist.step: Scope which roles are Schedule 2 functions
actions: Maintain the in-scope function list: directors, chief and deputy chief executives, senior executives performing controlled functions, shareholder controllers and the principal representative.
Map each in-scope function to its HRIS job profile so recruitment cannot start without the F&P flag set.
Review the list with the Chief HR Officer each January and on any reorganization.
Publish the list to HR and the Corporate Secretariat.
checklist.done: a current in-scope list exists, mapped to HRIS job profiles and published.

checklist.step: Open an F&P case at candidate or appointment intake
actions: When an in-scope role is offered or a board appointment proposed, open an F&P case naming the person, the function, the proposed effective date and the assessing counsel.
Block the HRIS start-date confirmation on the open case so the function cannot be assumed pre-clearance.
Issue the BMA-style personal questionnaire to the candidate with a 10-business-day return window.
Record consent for background checks in the case.
checklist.done: every in-scope offer has an open case, a blocked start date and an issued questionnaire.

checklist.step: Collect the candidate questionnaire and declarations
actions: Receive the completed questionnaire covering identity, employment history (10 years), directorships, regulatory history, criminal and civil matters, and financial soundness declarations.
Check every section is answered — no blanks accepted — and chase gaps within 3 business days.
Load the questionnaire to the case and index the person in the HRIS with the F&P flag pending.
Verify identity documents against the questionnaire details.
checklist.done: a complete, gap-free questionnaire with verified identity sits on the case.

checklist.step: Run the background verification set
actions: Order via the screening vendor: criminal record checks in each residence country (7 years), credit/financial soundness check, and directorship/disqualification searches.
Run sanctions and adverse-media screening on the person through the screening system and file the result.
Take up two professional references covering competence in the proposed function.
Verify claimed qualifications and professional memberships with the issuing bodies.
checklist.done: criminal, credit, sanctions, reference and qualification results are all on the case.

checklist.step: Verify regulatory history with prior regulators
actions: For candidates with prior regulated roles, check public registers (BMA enforcement notices, FCA register, NAIC RIRS or state actions as applicable) for findings against the person.
Record each register checked, the search date and the result, screenshotting nil returns.
Where a finding exists, obtain the underlying notice and refer it to Legal Counsel for materiality assessment.
File all captures on the case.
checklist.done: regulatory register checks are evidenced with dated captures and findings referred.

checklist.step: Score the assessment against the BMA fit-and-proper factors
actions: Assess the file against the three BMA limbs: probity (honesty, integrity, reputation), competence (knowledge, skills, experience for this function) and financial soundness.
Document the conclusion per limb with the evidence reference supporting it.
For adverse information, record the materiality analysis: relevance to the function, recency, pattern and candidate explanation.
Conclude fit, fit-with-conditions (naming them) or not fit.
checklist.done: a per-limb scored assessment with an explicit conclusion sits on the case.

checklist.step: Approve the appointment at the right gate
actions: Route fit conclusions for director and controller functions to General Counsel for countersignature; senior-executive conclusions to the Chief HR Officer and General Counsel jointly.
Reject any case where the function's effective date precedes the approval date — the date moves, not the control.
Record conditions attached to fit-with-conditions approvals and their monitoring owner.
Release the HRIS start-date block only on countersigned approval.
checklist.done: each appointment carries the required countersignatures before the start-date block lifts.

checklist.step: Obtain BMA approval where the function requires it
actions: Identify functions needing BMA no-objection or approval before appointment — principal representative changes and shareholder controller changes above notification thresholds.
Submit the application or notification through the BMA's electronic filing channel with the F&P evidence pack the BMA prescribes.
Hold the appointment until the BMA's no-objection or the statutory objection window passes.
File the BMA response on the case.
checklist.done: BMA-gated functions show the regulator's response filed before the function was assumed.

checklist.step: File the s.30 notification within 45 days
actions: On the appointment or cessation becoming effective, prepare the s.30 notification of the change of officer or controller.
File with the BMA within 45 days of the change, quoting the entity registration and effective date.
Diarize T-30 and T-40 alerts so the window cannot lapse silently.
Attach the BMA acknowledgement to the case and the director register.
checklist.done: each change shows an acknowledged notification filed inside 45 days.

checklist.step: Record the completed assessment in the person's F&P file
actions: Assemble the final file: questionnaire, checks, scoring memo, approvals, BMA correspondence and notification proof under REG-057/C13/<person>.
Apply restricted access limited to HR/Legal/Compliance named individuals and the 10-year post-departure retention label.
Set the HRIS F&P flag to cleared with the clearance date.
Close the case with the repository link recorded.
checklist.done: a complete restricted file exists, the HRIS flag shows cleared, and the case is closed with linkage.

checklist.step: Run the annual attestation refresh
actions: Each February, launch the attestation campaign to every in-scope function holder: confirm no new criminal, regulatory, financial-soundness or conflict matters since last attestation.
Chase non-responders weekly; escalate to the function holder's chair or manager at March 15.
Route any positive disclosure to Legal Counsel for reassessment within 10 business days.
Close the campaign by March 31 with a completion report to General Counsel.
checklist.done: all attestations are returned by March 31 with positive disclosures in reassessment.

checklist.step: Rescreen the standing population periodically
actions: Re-run sanctions and adverse-media screening over all in-scope function holders quarterly through the screening system.
Re-run criminal and credit checks on a 3-year cycle per person, tracked in the case system.
Route hits to Legal Counsel with the original file for delta assessment.
Record nil-return runs with date and population count.
checklist.done: quarterly screening and cyclical rechecks are evidenced across the whole in-scope population.

checklist.step: Reassess on adverse information at any time
actions: Open a reassessment case within 2 business days of adverse information arriving (self-disclosure, screening hit, regulator letter, press).
Re-score the affected limb with the new information and the person's response.
Decide retain, retain-with-conditions, suspend or remove, with General Counsel countersignature.
Notify the BMA where the finding means a minimum-criteria concern, coordinating wording with General Counsel.
checklist.done: every adverse event shows a reassessment with a countersigned decision and BMA notification where required.

checklist.step: Log and remediate F&P exceptions
actions: Raise an issue for any function assumed pre-clearance, missing file element, late notification or overdue attestation.
Assign root cause and a remediation owner in HR, Legal or the Secretariat.
Obtain General Counsel sign-off at closure.
Report open exceptions monthly to the Chief HR Officer and General Counsel.
checklist.done: every exception is tracked to a signed-off closure with monthly visibility.

checklist.step: Report programme status to the board
actions: Present an annual F&P report to the board: population count, assessments completed, attestation completion rate, adverse findings and dispositions.
Confirm in the report that the Schedule 2 fit-and-proper criterion is met, or state the gaps — this feeds the s.8A Declaration of Compliance.
Minute the board's acceptance and any directed actions.
File the report with the Declaration support file (REG-057-C12).
checklist.done: a minuted annual report exists and feeds the Declaration support file.

testing.step: Build the population of appointments and function holders
actions: Extract from the HRIS every hire, promotion or transfer into an F&P-flagged job profile during the year, with effective dates.
Extract the year-end standing population of in-scope function holders.
Add controller changes from the director register and share register.
testing.done: appointment-year and standing populations are extracted with effective dates.

testing.step: Reconcile the population for completeness
actions: Compare the HRIS in-scope extract to the Legal in-scope function list and the board portal's director register.
Identify any person performing a Schedule 2 function whose job profile lacks the F&P flag — a scoping failure.
List every unmatched person as an automatic exception.
testing.done: the three sources reconcile or scoping failures are listed as exceptions.

testing.step: Draw the sample
actions: Take 100% of director and controller appointments plus a seeded random sample of 10 senior-executive appointments, minimum 15 files.
Record seed, population size and selection date.
Include every adverse-information reassessment from the year.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all director/controller cases and reassessments is drawn.

testing.step: Verify clearance preceded function assumption
actions: For each sampled person, compare the countersigned approval date to the HRIS effective date and, for directors, the first meeting attended per minutes.
Any function assumed before approval is a reportable breach, not a test exception.
Verify the HRIS start-date block operated by checking the case closure timestamp preceded start confirmation.
testing.done: every sampled appointment shows approval strictly before assumption.

testing.step: Re-perform the evidence completeness check on sampled files
actions: Open each sampled F&P file and tick off: complete questionnaire, criminal check per residence country, credit check, sanctions screen, two references, qualification verification and regulatory register captures.
Verify the scoring memo addresses all three BMA limbs with evidence references.
List any missing element per file as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled file is element-complete with a three-limb scoring memo or gaps are listed.

testing.step: Re-perform one scoring judgement
actions: For the sampled file with the most adverse information, re-read the raw checks and reach an independent fit/not-fit view before reading the scoring memo.
Compare conclusions; a divergence on materiality goes to General Counsel for adjudication.
Document the re-performance reasoning in the workpaper.
testing.done: an independent re-scoring exists with divergences adjudicated.

testing.step: Recompute s.30 notification timeliness
actions: For every officer/controller change in the year, recompute days from effective date to BMA notification date.
Compare against the 45-day window; verify BMA acknowledgements exist.
List late or unacknowledged notifications as exceptions.
testing.done: all notification day-counts are recomputed with lates listed.

testing.step: Test the attestation campaign and periodic rescreening
actions: Verify the March 31 attestation completion report against the standing population — every holder attested or escalated.
Sample two quarterly sanctions-screening runs and verify the screened population equalled the in-scope list on the run date.
Trace one positive disclosure to its reassessment case and disposition.
testing.done: attestation completeness and screening coverage verify with disclosures traced.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the person-anonymized file id, the function and the failed attribute.
Assign root cause (scoping miss, evidence gap, timing breach, campaign gap) and an owner.
Route any pre-clearance assumption or unfit-person finding to General Counsel same-day.
Set remediation dates and carry open items to next year's test.
testing.done: all exceptions are tracked with root cause, owner and required escalations.

testing.step: Conclude with independent sign-off
actions: State the conclusion against the zero pre-clearance-assumption and zero late-notification thresholds.
Have the Chief Audit Executive, outside HR and Legal, sign the workpaper.
Report to the audit committee and General Counsel ahead of the annual board F&P report.
File the workpaper under REG-057/C13/testing.
testing.done: a signed conclusion is filed and reported before the board F&P report.
